cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: A Kinder Version
cards.instruction: Protect someone from the full truth by offering a carefully edited explanation that feels kinder than complete honesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. The gallery thinks your portrait would suit a more adventurous exhibition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're showing a fridge full of teeth. What did they say about mine?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. That the face doesn't immediately reveal what you intended.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's you. They called it unrecognisable, didn't they?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They think knowing the sitter would help. I'll attend your next opening with a matching shirt.

mechanism: A protects its painting pupil from rejection by translating hostile feedback into an advanced training need and volunteering a practical aid rather than naming the insult.
confusable: Not simple praise: A keeps editing an increasingly explicit criticism into something the pupil can act on.
comparison: Protecting creative confidence versus cushioning social exclusion.
